questions.question: What is 'tie capacity'? The source says it is the 'rated capacity' (a static nameplate rating) but also says it arrives from the SCADA scan every 10 s (a live value, usually the alternate feeder's spare capacity). Which is it, and in which unit: kW (what the code uses today), kVA or A (feeders carry rating_amps)? If it is kVA or A, what power factor or voltage converts the load_kw load basis, and what p.u. base should the tolerance use?
When is a 10 s scan value 'late' (for example 20 s = 2 missed scans, or 30 s)? Inside that window, may the planner hold the last good value, or must it refuse any value older than one scan?

Today tie_capacity_kw is a bare dict[str, float] with no timestamp or quality. How should the value's timestamp and SCADA quality reach build_plan and POST /flisr/plan? May we extend the build_plan signature and the POST /flisr/plan body (an API change for the SCADA adapter), and who owns the adapter side?
When transferred load exactly equals tie capacity, should the tie close or not? Is a safety margin or comparison tolerance needed, stated in kW and p.u.?

The source says 'the plan must say so instead of restoring'. When one tie's capacity is unknown, is only that tie blocked (the lockout reclose and ties with known capacity still go ahead), or is the whole restoration refused (isolation-only / manual-action plan, or HTTP 409)? Must 'capacity unknown' also be a machine-readable RestorationPlan field, not only a free-text note?
When load exceeds capacity, should the planner try a partial pick-up (open a downstream sectionalizer so the rest fits), or is skipping the tie the required outcome? Skipping is today's behaviour.

When two or more ties pick up load from the same alternate feeder, is capacity per tie, or shared so that the sum of the transfers must fit? The shipped model has one tie, so the source does not settle this.

The brief's layer map names backend/app/state_estimation.py and backend/app/main.py, but those files do not exist; the real files are state_estimator.py and api.py. The source also names locate_fault as the planner, but the capacity logic is in build_plan. answer: CAPACITY_INVALID = kw is NaN, +/-inf, negative, or not a finite number, or the timestamp is unparseable/timezone-naive/future-dated (see Q-SPEC-10). A quality other than GOOD is CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (same as missing). Precedence when several apply, evaluate in this order and report the first: CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED. Malformed HTTP input (wrong types, unknown fields) is rejected by request validation with HTTP 422 and never reaches the planner.

Time reference is the request's as_of field: a timezone-aware ISO-8601 UTC instant supplied by the caller; when absent the server uses UTC now and echoes the value it used in the response. Capacity timestamps must be timezone-aware; naive timestamps are CAPACITY_INVALID. A timestamp more than 2 s ahead of as_of is CAPACITY_INVALID. Age = as_of - timestamp.

The new body field tie_capacity (dict[str, TieCapacity]) and the legacy tie_capacity_kw are mutually exclusive; both present is HTTP 422. Legacy-only requests are treated as quality GOOD with timestamp = as_of and the response carries deprecations: ['tie_capacity_kw']. The deprecation note lives in the endpoint's OpenAPI description and in the docs page the Document stage produces; removal is a separate change after one release.

questions.question: Invalid as_of. Q-SPEC-10 only covers a missing as_of. What happens when the supplied as_of is (a) timezone-naive, (b) aware but with a non-UTC offset such as +02:00 (accept it as the same instant, or reject?), or (c) unparseable? The two options are: reject with HTTP 422, so no plan and not even isolation; or build the plan with isolation and block every candidate tie as CAPACITY_INVALID. (d) Should a supplied as_of be bounded against the server clock? Without a bound, a caller can back-date as_of so that stale capacity looks fresh, which bypasses the 20 s staleness rule.

Unparseable capacity timestamp over HTTP. Q-SPEC-9 says an unparseable timestamp is CAPACITY_INVALID (per tie, HTTP 200) and that wrong types get HTTP 422 for the whole request. In JSON the timestamp is a string either way, so is a non-ISO-8601 string such as 'yesterday' (a) a per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID with HTTP 200, which means TieCapacity.timestamp must accept any string, or (b) a 422? And is a JSON number (Unix seconds) a wrong type (422) or accepted?

answer: (a) timezone-naive as_of: HTTP 422. (b) aware non-UTC offset: accept, normalise to the same UTC instant. (c) unparseable: HTTP 422. (d) yes, bounded: an as_of more than 60 s before or 2 s after the server clock is HTTP 422, so staleness cannot be bypassed by back-dating. 422 means no plan at all, which is acceptable because the request itself is malformed; the operator retries with a valid request.

(b) 422. TieCapacity.timestamp is a strict timezone-aware ISO-8601 datetime field; a non-ISO string or a JSON number is a request-validation failure for the whole request. Per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID for timestamps therefore covers only well-formed values that fail the semantic rules (future-dated beyond 2 s). Q-SPEC-9 is amended to match.

questions.question: A section with negative Section.load_kw (e.g. DG export) inside a candidate set whose total L is still >= 0 makes L understate the load the tie would actually carry (measured: spur -600 kW, C=1000 -> closes at L=890 kW while the non-negative loads total 1490 kW). Draft PR #13 (DEF-FLISR-7) holds a candidate tie open with a note and no blocked_ties entry, which contradicts REQ-TIECAP-21 ('every candidate tie not closed appears exactly once in blocked_ties'). Pick one: (a) ties held open by the DEF-FLISR-7 guard are not candidate ties for REQ-TIECAP-11/18/21; the guard runs before L and the verdict (recommended); (b) add a fifth BlockedTie reason, e.g. BACKFEED_FAULTED_SECTION, ahead of CAPACITY_INVALID (changes Q-SPEC-5 enum, REQ-TIECAP-9/11); (c) fix a merge order and let the second change amend its own requirements.

answer: A negative, NaN or infinite section load is invalid model data, not a load to net off. build_plan refuses the whole plan (FlisrError, HTTP 409, lockout stays open) when any candidate section's load_kw is not a finite non-negative number; L is otherwise the plain sum. This is covered by the out-of-range precondition and needs no change to REQ-TIECAP-3/21; record it in the design as a stated precondition and add a test vector.

Draft PR #13 (DEF-FLISR-7 hold-open guard) lands first and is kept. Design on top of it: a tie refused because its pick-up set touches the faulted section is reported in blocked_ties with a new reason FAULTED_SECTION, evaluated before every capacity reason (precedence FAULTED_SECTION > CAPACITY_INVALID > CAPACITY_UNKNOWN > CAPACITY_STALE > CAPACITY_EXCEEDED). REQ-TIECAP-21 is amended accordingly in the spec by the Design stage (note the amendment in design.md and the trace); the guard's behaviour must not change.
